description: Use case: does the delay of an intervention decide whether disinformation can be answered at all? The file collects the measured latencies of current interventions (community notes on X, removals on Facebook and X, takedowns under the DSA) against the speed of the spread (repost half-life, saturation time), the simulated effect of an intervention as a function of its delay (Bak-Coleman 2022, Truong 2025), and the argument of a forum dialogue that with generative AI the effort asymmetry between publishing and refuting has grown so far that Popper's condition for tolerance, the possibility of counter-speech, no longer holds; the thesis of symmetric hiding is stored as an assumption with its confidence. No study has tested the symmetric case empirically; the simulations vary the delay as a parameter, the field studies measure the asymmetry of today.

sources.name: Bak-Coleman 2022
sources.description: Bak-Coleman J.B., Kennedy I., Wack M., Beers A., Schafer J.S., Spiro E.S., Starbird K., West J.D. (2022). Combining interventions to reduce the spread of viral misinformation. Nature Human Behaviour 6:1372-1380. Generative branching-process model of viral spread fitted to 10.5 million Twitter posts from 454 misinformation events of the 2020 US election; simulates removal after a delay, virality circuit breakers, nudges, account removal and their combination. Open access.

sources.name: Chuai 2026
sources.description: Chuai Y., Pilarski M., Renault T., Restrepo-Amariles D., Troussel-Clément A., Lenzini G., Pröllochs N. (2026). Community-based fact-checking reduces the spread of misleading posts on X (formerly Twitter). Nature Communications 17:4070. Difference-in-differences on minute-level repost time series of 237180 community fact-checked cascades, 6 October 2022 to 11 June 2024. Open access.

sources.name: Vosoughi 2018
sources.description: Vosoughi S., Roy D., Aral S. (2018). The spread of true and false news online. Science 359:1146-1151. About 126000 rumour cascades spread by about 3 million people on Twitter 2006-2017, rated by six fact-checking organisations.

sources.name: Truong 2025
sources.description: Truong B.T., Kim S., Nogara G., Verdolotti E., Samieyan Sahneh E., Saurwein F., Just N., Luceri L., Giordano S., Menczer F. (2025). Audit of takedown delays across social media reveals failure to reduce exposure to illegal content. arXiv:2502.08841. Audit of statements of reasons in the DSA transparency database for 2024 on five platforms plus the agent-based model SimSoM calibrated to the measured delays. Preprint.

sources.name: Goldstein 2023
sources.description: Goldstein I., Edelson L., Nguyen M.-K., Goga O., McCoy D., Lauinger T. (2023). Understanding the (in)effectiveness of content moderation: a case study of Facebook in the context of the U.S. Capitol riot. arXiv:2301.02737. Removed posts of US news publishers on Facebook around 6 January 2021 and the engagement they had gathered before removal. Preprint.

sources.name: Shahi 2025
sources.description: Shahi G.K., Mejova Y. (2025). Too little, too late: moderation of misinformation around the Russo-Ukrainian conflict. arXiv:2502.18500. 500 tweets identified as misinformation by 41 fact-checking organisations, a streaming sample of 543475 of their retweets, and the platform status of the tweets re-queried in May 2024. Preprint.

sources.name: arXiv 2509.11052
sources.description: Fact-checking comments precede community notes to misleading posts on X (2025). arXiv:2509.11052. Language-model pipeline over 2.2 million comments under 1841 community fact-checked misleading posts, comparing the timing of organic fact-checking comments with the creation and display of community notes. Preprint; author list not verified.

sources.name: Popper 1945
sources.description: Popper K.R. (1945). The Open Society and Its Enemies, volume 1: The Spell of Plato, chapter 7, note 4. Routledge. The paradox of tolerance: tolerance should not be extended to the intolerant if they refuse rational argument and answer it with force.

sources.name: forum dialogue 2026-09
sources.description: Dialogue in a newspaper comment forum, September 2026, between the author of this file and another commenter, prompted by the Arte series 'Stimmt das?', episode 'Durfte man früher mehr sagen?' (from minute 20: censorship by disinformation). The commenter holds that freedom of expression outweighs any censorship and that only organised foreign disinformation may justify limits; the author holds that hiding must become as fast and easy as publishing. The assumed values of this file come from that dialogue.
